messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] Canary health check failing for rollout 'release/2026-03-15' in eu-west-1. error-rate > 8% on /v1/generate, latency p95 2.3s. Paging oncall.

deploy-bot: Started canary rollout to 5% traffic at 23:07 UTC. config: model=redwood-v2-embed, batch_policy=aggressive, quant=qt8.

jordan: seeing steady 503s, spiky 429s from the canary pool. I'm pausing the rollout but traffic still routing. Anyone oncall?

maya: oncall, joining. jordan what's the canary tag? I will check routing rules.

jordan: tag release/2026-03-15-canary. I ran `rctl rollout status release/2026-03-15` and it returned:
```
Canary: 5% active
instances healthy: 3/12
503 spikes on instances: i-0a12, i-0b34
prefix cache hit drop by 12%
```

maya: digging into logs. k8s pod kube-proxy looks fine. suspect kernel OOM on quantized variant. kyle, any kernel/quant patches applied recently?

kyle: pushed a micro-optim change to quant runtime last week but only to main-distro, not hf branch. Not seeing global alerts. Can you dump model-variant logs? Also check KV cache fills.

samir: I see a correlated increase in KV cache misses on the canary prefix keys. Could be a cache eviction policy interacting with quantized kernels.

jordan: customer impact: some latency increases and error spikes for a subset of EU requests hitting new variant. No full outage. Affected endpoints: /v1/generate (streaming), /v1/chat. Low % of users (~3%) affected but high error rate.

maya: given risk, recommend immediate feature-flag flip to route away from canary and activate fallback variant. I'll flip the control-plane flag.

maya: flipping flag now: `ffctl set route.release-2026-03-15 canary=false` -> response: OK.

deploy-bot: Traffic steering policy updated: release/2026-03-15 canary removed from weighted routing. Traffic diverted to main stable variants.

incident-bot: NOTE: automatic fallback engaged. Monitoring for 10m to confirm stabilization.

jordan: after flag flip, errors dropped within 90s. p95 latency back to baseline 420ms. Good. We should still roll back the canary images and open a revert PR.

kyle: I will snapshot failing instances and collect kernel logs. Command:
```
ssh root@i-0a12 'journalctl -u redwood-runtime | tail -n 500' > /tmp/i-0a12-rt.log
scp /tmp/i-0a12-rt.log logs-storage:/incidents/2375012345/
```

samir: capturing KV cache metrics, will attach to incident doc. Initial hypothesis: aggressive batching + qt8 quant combined with cache churn causing OOM/retry loops on certain low-memory hosts.

maya: Starting formal mitigation runbook:
- hunt for suspicious process restarts (maya)
- rollback canary images from registry to previous digest (kyle)
- open bug with runtime team (jordan)
- notify customer success for any noisy accounts (samir)

jordan: I opened a revert PR: `github.com/redwood/release/PR#6421` — build pinned to digest sha256:abcd1234. Please review and merge ASAP if we decide to roll back fully.

kyle: reverted canary image tags and scaled down canary replica set to 0. Command used:
```
kubectl scale rs release-2026-03-15-canary --replicas=0 -n model-serving
```

deploy-bot: Canary replica set scaled to 0. All new canary instances terminated gracefully.

maya: handoff to night SRE in 20m. Jordan, please include a short summary for the handoff and link to logs/PR.

jordan: Handoff summary for on-call night team:
- What happened: Canary release to eu-west caused 503/429 spikes on 5% traffic due to interaction between qt8 quant kernel and aggressive batching; KV cache miss rate spiked.
- Impact: ~3% of EU users saw errors and increased latency for /v1/generate and /v1/chat. No data corruption.
- Mitigation done: Flipped route flag to remove canary, scaled canary replicas to 0, opened revert PR and collected logs.
- Action items: runtime team to triage kernel OOM traces (kyle), QA to reproduce with qt8+aggressive batching, consider emergency patch to quant runtime or relax batch_policy.
- Links: logs: logs-storage/incidents/2375012345/, PR: github.com/redwood/release/PR#6421

maya: copying to #incidents and ops-runbook. samir please loop in customer-success for any customers who reported errors.

samir: pinged customer-success. They acknowledged and will prepare outreach if any paying customers escalate.

incident-bot: Incident 2375012345 severity lowered to P3 after mitigation. Continue monitoring for 1 hour.

kyle: grabbing core dumps and kernel traces now. If we confirm an OOM pattern we may need to revert qt8 profile for that hardware class.

jordan: thanks all. I'll stay awake for the monitoring window and will update if anything regresses. Maya — handing off to you in 20.

maya: acknowledged. I'll take final checks and create a concise post-incident note for postmortem. leaving contact: maya (pager) if anything pops.

jordan: handing off — shifting to watch mode. All clear for now.:thumbsup:

maya: closing on-call thread for handoff. please add any new artefacts to the incident folder.
